recipes.ws4_note: Target scaling chosen in WS4: ratio. Compared raw / asinh / ratio-to-trailing-level on five TRAIN folds, confirmed on 2024.

scaling_caveat.finding: The ratio transform's advantage is DRIFT-DEPENDENT, not constant.
scaling_caveat.evidence: Across five TRAIN-internal rolling-origin windows the advantage over raw tracks the level drift of the evaluation window almost perfectly (correlation +0.987): +1.30% at 13.5% drift rising to +24.14% at 84.1% drift. DEV has 81.7% drift, and a line fitted on the TRAIN windows alone predicts +21.83% there against a measured +25.73%.
scaling_caveat.how_to_quote: Quote the 55.92% DEV skill as conditional on a high-drift period. In a flat-level period expect the advantage over raw to be small (~1-2%), not 26%.
scaling_caveat.why_still_adopted: The advantage was POSITIVE in every window tested, including the lowest-drift one. The transform is regime-dependent in magnitude but not in sign, so adopting it has a small-positive floor rather than a downside.

We record this openly because on this budget line the published model is not the single best 2024 number.

gate_policy.note: Gate verdicts and the publication decision are DERIVED, not hand-written. This block and every dev_credentials.gates entry is the output of publication_gates.decide() on the logged measurements; test_publication_gates.py asserts they agree.
gate_policy.mase_rationale: MASE is a ratio against a TRAIN-only seasonal-naive benchmark, so 1.0 is the definitional break-even rather than a chosen constant. Above it, a documented trivial alternative is more accurate.
gate_policy.sentinel_rationale: Calibrated against a measured null distribution: 360 draws, false-positive rate 0.00% at 1.15 and 0.56% at 1.10, null max 1.1164. The old 1.50 also had FPR 0.00% and therefore bought no extra protection while rejecting real readings.
gate_policy.vs_ruler_rationale: Demoted to a reported diagnostic. Its threshold was '> 0%', which a featureless constant clears by 38.58% on Revenues; and it cannot be raised to a fixed number because the same constant scores -299.43% on the stock target.
